Subject: Capacity concerns ahead of renewal — can we rebaseline?

Camila,

Quick note from the Nemesis infra/ML team — our Q4 traffic is trending higher than forecasted and the live inference fleet hit sustained peaks last week. We’ll be up for renewal in 3 weeks and want to understand options for: (a) adjusting our committed Dedicated capacity without a full-term increase, and (b) short-term burst capacity to cover Black Friday style peaks.

A couple of specifics from our telemetry (attached snapshot):
- 7d avg GPU utilization: 62%
- 95th percentile hourly utilization: 94% (three spike days last week)
- Peak request latency increased ~18% during spikes (tail p95->p99)

We’d like a concrete proposal that ties commit sizing to utilization and explains how burst tranches would be billed. Also include lead times for adding GPUs and any SLA impact. Procurement is looped on cc — they’ll need pricing line items and a POable invoice.

Thanks,
Anna Chu
VP, ML Ops — Nemesis.ai

Anna — thanks for the clear data. We can absolutely structure the renewal to reduce your risk. High level recommendation below; attached is a short tranche pricing workbook and a draft mutual action plan.

Summary recommendation (two-option approach):

Option A — Rebaseline + Burst (recommended)
- Move baseline commit: +6 A100-equivalent GPUs (effective sustained capacity) — expected to bring target utilization down to ~70% assuming current traffic.
- Add a configurable burst tranche: +8 GPUs available on-demand for up to 48 hours, billed at burst hourly rate or amortized into a monthly reservation credit if used >120 hours/month.
- Lead time: baseline GPUs provisioned within 7 business days after contract amendment; burst tranche available within 24 hours once enabled.
- SLA: no change to uptime SLA; tail latency SLO improved by routing burst traffic to burst pool.

Option B — Short-term commit bump (minimal ops change)
- Add +10 GPUs to baseline commit for the renewal term. Simpler billing but higher monthly cost. Provisioning lead time ~10 business days.

Telemetry rationale:
- We observed sustained 62% average utilization with frequent peaks to 94%; target utilization for stable latency is ~65–75% for your workload given sequence lengths and KV cache hit profiles. The +6 baseline +8 burst lets you keep average unit economics close to current while protecting tail latency.

Pricing delta (summary):
- Option A incremental baseline: $12,500/mo for +6 GPUs; burst tranche hourly: $45/hr per GPU when used.
- Option B incremental baseline: $18,900/mo for +10 GPUs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal confirmation on capacity roadmap (cc’d KarThik).
2) We update the renewal paperwork with either Option A or B.
3) If Option A chosen, we prepare an addendum to enable burst and a billing rule for amortized burst credits.

I’ve attached: proposed_tranche_pricing.xlsx and mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf. Happy to run a quick 20-min call to walk through numbers.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
